geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Archimedes' squeeze on a circle of diameter 1; note Lambert proved pi irrational in 1761.

Goal: I can explain how inscribed and circumscribed polygon perimeters trap the circumference, and state that pi is irrational, so 3.14 and 22/7 are only approximations.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
For a circle of diameter 1, every inscribed polygon's perimeter is less than the circumference, and every circumscribed polygon's perimeter is greater. As the number of sides grows, the two perimeters squeeze together. The number they close in on is the circumference of a circle with diameter 1, called π.

Archimedes used 96-gons to show 3 10/71 < π < 3 1/7. In 1761 Lambert proved π is irrational: its decimals never end or repeat. So 3.14 and 22/7 are approximations only.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
A student says: Pi equals 22/7 or 3.14 exactly.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.
